purpose: Add an upstream genetic and experimentally induced variant layer to the cross-dementia brain-insulin temporal analysis.
model_ordering_rule: Prepend Model 0 before Models 1-5. Model 0 is an etiologic/susceptibility model and does not replace the downstream mechanistic models.

model_0.name: genetic_susceptibility_and_variant_induction
model_0.title: Genetic susceptibility and experimentally induced variant model
model_0.summary: Inherited common variants, polygenic architecture, rare/pathogenic variants, and experimentally introduced variants may alter insulin/IGF signaling, cellular metabolism, or susceptibility to metabolic stress before clinical dementia, with effects that may be shared across dementias or disease-specific.
core_questions: Do dementia-risk variants alter brain insulin signaling or insulin responsiveness before overt neurodegeneration?
Do type-2-diabetes, insulin-resistance, glycemic, adiposity, or metabolic-risk variants modify risk, age at onset, pathology, progression, or insulin-signaling phenotype in specific dementias?
Are there shared variants, loci, genes, pathways, eQTLs, pQTLs, sQTLs, or polygenic components linking insulin biology and more than one dementia?
Are observed genetic overlaps causal, pleiotropic, mediated, confounded by linkage disequilibrium, or ancestry-specific?
Can introduction or correction of a variant in an isogenic preclinical system induce or rescue an insulin-signaling phenotype?
Does the same variant produce the same insulin phenotype across neurons, astrocytes, microglia, endothelium, and different dementia-pathology backgrounds?

genetic_evidence_classes.G0_constitutive_genotype: Genotype is present from conception. This establishes temporal availability of susceptibility only, not onset of the functional insulin phenotype.
G5_causal_inference: mechanism-specific genetic instruments for insulin sensitivity, beta-cell function, glycemia, adiposity, lipids, inflammation, or vascular traits
mediation analyses where assumptions are defensible
G6_variant_to_function_experiment: patient-derived iPSC models carrying natural variants
crosses between dementia-pathology models and insulin-pathway manipulations
induced metabolic stress or insulin-challenge experiments stratified by genotype

variant_directions_to_test.definition: Dementia-risk genotype changes insulin/IGF signaling or metabolic response.
Genetic liability to insulin resistance, diabetes, glycemia, adiposity, or related metabolic traits changes dementia risk or trajectory.
The same locus or pathway independently influences both dementia biology and metabolic/insulin biology.
Dementia genotype modifies the effect of systemic metabolic exposure, or metabolic genotype modifies dementia-pathology effects.

preclinical_variant_requirements.preferred_design: isogenic variant introduction or correction with matched background
preclinical_variant_requirements.strongest_causal_pattern: Introduce a variant into an isogenic control and induce the phenotype, then correct/revert the variant and rescue the phenotype, preferably across independent clones and with functional insulin stimulation.
do_not_equate: dementia pathology in a transgenic model with a genetically caused insulin phenotype
a constitutive genotype with early functional pathway activation

predictions: If a shared upstream genetic mechanism exists, cross-dementia genetic analyses should identify reproducible shared loci or pathways linked specifically to insulin/metabolic signaling.
If effects are disease-specific, variant-to-insulin phenotypes should depend on dementia genotype/pathology background or cell type.
If metabolic genetic liability is causal, genetically predicted insulin-resistance-related traits should influence dementia outcomes under pleiotropy-robust analyses.
If genetic overlap is noncausal pleiotropy, shared loci may exist without consistent mediation through insulin signaling.
Isogenic introduction/correction experiments should provide stronger variant-to-function evidence than non-isogenic case-control cellular comparisons.

temporal_integration.principle: Genetic susceptibility and functional phenotype onset are separate clocks.
temporal_integration.claim_rule: Never state that a pathway begins at birth merely because the risk genotype is present at birth. Report inherited susceptibility as temporally antecedent, while functional insulin-signaling onset remains independently estimated.

bias_and_validity_checks: batch and clone effects in iPSC models
developmental compensation in constitutive knockout models
